messages:
Priya: Quick sync: the new int4 microquant canary in staging is producing a weird class of funcall outputs — valid JSON but with broken escape sequences inside string args, causing downstream callers to mis-interpret tool params. Fail rate ~2.6% on funcall-heavy workload (3k samples).

Sam: Can you paste an example?

Priya: Sure — from a failing trace:
```
{"tool":"lookup","args":{"id":"user\\u000Aname=\"jin\"","filters":["active"]}}
```
Note: the sequence `\\u000A` should be a literal escaped newline token inside the JSON string, but streaming cut converted it to a raw control char in some chunks. Parser accepts JSON but the tool sees an actual newline in the arg.

Ava: Interesting: fp16 parity set showed 0.02% of this class. So it's strongly correlated with microquant. Could be tokenization boundary shifts causing escape sequences to be split across stream frames.

Marta: Risk: our client retry behavior currently retries on parse exceptions, but here the parse succeeds and tooling executes with corrupted arg. That means retries won't help and we can silently do bad side-effects.

Jin: Suggestion: add a post-emit validator that checks for non-printable/control chars in tool arg strings and rejects (or quarantines) those responses for manual review. For quarantined responses, return a safe error to the client and do not invoke the tool.

Sam: +1 on quarantining side-effectful ops. We can add idempotency tokens for all tool-invoke HTTP calls so retries become safe for read-only tools. But we need a manifest marking which tools are side-effectful.

Priya: Operational plan: 1) deploy a thin sanitizer that scans emitted JSON for control chars (regex: /[\x00-\x1F&&[^\n\t]]/) and either mark repairable or quarantine. 2) log original raw stream + token cutpoints to telemetry. 3) run an A/B for 24h: group A (new int4 + sanitizer in quarantine mode), group B (old fp16 baseline).

Ava: For (1) if it's repairable (only missing escapes or unbalanced quotes), we can attempt conservative repairs but tag them as repaired_success and surface diffs in telemetry. Don't auto-fix anything that changes semantics (e.g., converts escaped newline to real newline).

Marta: I'm adding telemetry dims: model_variant, parsed_ok, quarantined, repaired, repair_ops (list), tool_name, invoked_flag, idempotency_token. Also add a hist of tool latency split by quarantined vs normal.

Sam: Implementation note: sanitizer and quarantine should live in the postprocess service (not the runtime) so we can iterate quickly without touching the serving kernel. Keep it sync: if quarantined, return 400-like structured error with code "TOOL_QUARANTINED".

Jin: For experiments, I propose running a targeted eval of 20k historical tool-call prompts through the int4 model offline and compute a repair-vs-quarantine taxonomy before any rollout. That gives us expected SLO impact.

Priya: I'll run that eval tonight and upload a CSV to the shared drive. If quarantine rate >1% for critical tools, we hold the canary.

deploy-bot: queued: `int4-sanitizer-quarantine-v1` -> staging. CI: 2/4 tasks passing.

Ava: Also, add an alert: increase in quarantined for any tool >0.5% in a 5m window triggers a canary hold.

Marta: I'll wire the alert and add a short runbook: check token cut logs, run offline repair heuristics, escalate to model on-call if repairs > 30% of quarantines.

Sam: I'll push the token-cut logger and the quarantine response payload shape by 10:00 PT. Priya, share the eval results when ready.

Priya: Will do. Thanks everyone.
